result.title: TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates
result.summary: Degree certificates play a critical role in high-stakes decisions such as university admission, immigration, and hiring. The issuing institution vouches for the holder, so a forged certificate may let its bearer pass these checks. Degree certificate forgery is increasingly prevalent. Yet, many assume that it is easy to spot. Reported cases show otherwise: in 2024, the business school of the University of Hong Kong found that about 30 master's students had enrolled with forged academic credentials. Few studies have looked at how to detect forged degree certificates, partly because public benchmarks are scarce. We present TamperCert, a benchmark built from 400 real degree certificates issued by 38 universities. Each certificate was subjected to 11 publicly available tampering methods to alter the holder's name and further processed with four additional post-processing techniques, resulting in over 20,000 forged images. We evaluate 13 detectors, a commercial multimodal large language model (MLLM), and detectors trained on TamperCert.Our findings reveal that no detector is reliable for every tampering method. Consequently, a determined forger may still evade detection. Moreover, the commercial MLLM misses most forgeries made by general-purpose generative models, and post-processing, such as resizing an image or photographing it with a camera, severely degrades detection.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建 TamperCert 基准：基于 400 份真实学位证书、38 所高校，用 11 种公开篡改方法与 4 种后处理生成两万余张伪造图像，并评测 13 种检测器及一个商用 MLLM；结果显示没有检测器对全部篡改方式可靠，MLLM 对通用生成模型伪造漏检严重，缩放与拍照后处理显著削弱检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 该研究并非 LVR 推理研究，但其关于 MLLM 对细粒度视觉篡改漏检、后处理破坏局部证据的负结果，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留与证据筛选评价的薄弱环节。
